paper.title_en: Primordial B-mode sensitivity forecasts for northern-sky cosmic microwave background surveys
paper.abstract_en: Northern-sky cosmic microwave background (CMB) polarization observations offer additional sky coverage and independent measurements in the search for primordial gravitational waves. We assess their potential through idealized sensitivity forecasts motivated by the Ali CMB Polarization Telescope. Using a power-spectrum likelihood and Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling, we relate assumed map depths, accessible angular scales, and effective sky coverage to constraints on the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$. The model retains lensing B modes and assumes negligible residual foreground power. A benchmark with 95 and 150\,GHz channels, a polarization map depth of $40\,μ\mathrm{K\,arcmin}$ per channel, and $f_{\rm sky}=0.1$ yields $σ(r)=0.023$ for a fiducial $r=0.014$, improving to 0.015 with Planck-like mock data. At a per-channel depth of $10\,μ\mathrm{K\,arcmin}$, the northern survey alone reaches $σ(r)=0.0031$. Raising the minimum multipole from 30 to 70 degrades the baseline sensitivity to 0.037, while extending the effective area at fixed depth improves the constraint. As the northern maps deepen, their contribution increasingly determines the precision on $r$, whereas Planck-like information continues to constrain the scalar spectral index. These forecasts quantify the scope for improved northern-sky tensor constraints and establish sensitivity benchmarks for subsequent studies of joint northern and southern CMB observations.
